transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12 08:00 PT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood CSM), Dr. Lian Chen (HelixMed), Marcus Nguyen (HelixMed), Priya Rao (HelixMed)

AutoSummary: quick POC check-in; reviewed latest metrics; compared three candidate model variants from Redwood catalog; agreed to run a controlled rollback dry-run and share security pack.

00:00 Jordan Park: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, should be about 45ish minutes, quick agenda — brief results review, model selector matrix, and then a dry-run plan for rollback and fallback, ok?
00:28 Priya Rao: yep sounds good, we have two execs heads down but Lian and Marcus will run the details, thanks.
01:12 Sofia Martinez: cool, i'll start with the numbers we ran last week — table's in the sheet Jordan shared, but highlights: we tested three variants: rwd-7b-q4 (fast/quant), rwd-13b-fp16 (balanced), and rwd-30b-int8 (highest quality). latency at 25 qps with KV cache on — median 85ms for 7b, 180ms for 13b, 420ms for 30b. 95th/99th tails are attached in the histogram tab.
02:05 Dr. Lian Chen: quick question, those tails look pretty spiky for the 30b — is that on our dev trace or the synthetic prompts?
02:22 Sofia Martinez: it's a replay of your 2k representative prompts you uploaded last week, so realistic. we saw that the 30b suffers from occasional kernel fallback which increases tails. also note token cost per response went up by ~3x compared to 7b.
03:10 Marcus Nguyen: can you explain kernel fallback, is that like oom or CUDA retries?
03:20 Sofia Martinez: mm yeah it's mostly work-stealing between compute lanes and occasionally a slower kernel path triggered by long sequence length or kv cache miss; sometimes the runtime will fall back to a compatibility kernel which slows things. we can mitigate with shorter max-seq or different compilation flags.
04:05 Jordan Park: and just to frame it from HelixMed's SLOs — you told us 95p latency should be under 250ms for interactive triage flows?
04:18 Dr. Lian Chen: correct, for clinician-facing UIs we want sub-250ms 95p, and for batch reports 95p under 1s is fine. also anything that touches PHI must not leave our VPC and needs KMS-managed keys.
05:00 Jordan Park: got it. that drives us toward either 13b pinned with optimizations or a hybrid: 7b for triage path and 30b in background for longer form, with an automatic soft-fallback.
05:38 Priya Rao: remind me of cost delta between Dedicated and Hosted for those patterns?
05:48 Jordan Park: high-level: hosted per-token cost is higher but zero infra ops; Dedicated reserved capacity reduces unit cost around 40-60% depending on commit, and gives you predictable throughput and VPC peering. we'll send a dedicated pricing sheet after.
06:25 Dr. Lian Chen: ok on model selection — we want to avoid noisy fallbacks that flip users mid-response. what does Redwood recommend for version pinning and soft fallback?
06:42 Sofia Martinez: two patterns we use: hard pin — route 100% to a named model version, and soft fallback — shadow routing plus a circuit-breaker that triggers fallback to a smaller compatible variant if latency or error rate crosses thresholds. the selector matrix we're proposing maps intent->model, e.g., 'clinical-triage' -> rwd-7b-q4 pinned, 'synthesis' -> rwd-30b-int8 with 10% shadow to 13b for regression checks.
07:50 Marcus Nguyen: is shadowing stateful? will kv cache warm across shadow requests?
08:03 Sofia Martinez: currently shadow requests are cold and do not share KV with primary traffic; we can run a warm-shadow experiment but that requires session affinity and additional runtime config. warm-shadow will give better comparability but is heavier.
09:00 Jordan Park: quick pause — competitors question came up in procurement; HelixMed asked if Anthropic or OpenAI offer something similar for dedicated VPC + guaranteed tail latencies?
09:18 Ethan Cole: short answer: others have managed endpoints but our differentiator is the model catalog + runtime-level batching and KV cache controls that let you optimize unit economics without sacrificing SLOs. procurement usually cares about SLAs, and we'll map our SLOs in the contract.
10:05 Dr. Lian Chen: back to dry-run — what does a rollback dry-run look like operationally? we want to test the path where a new model deploy causes a 2x spike and we want to cut to fallback automatically.
10:25 Sofia Martinez: propose this sequence — (1) deploy candidate as canary at 10%; (2) impose a synthetic traffic spike via our test harness for 10 minutes to push latency to threshold; (3) trigger the circuit-breaker based on 95p > X ms or error rate Y%; (4) validate traffic routes to fallback model and observe latency and correctness; (5) roll forward once metrics stabilize. we'll coordinate runbook steps and a play-by-play.
11:40 Marcus Nguyen: what thresholds do you normally use?
11:48 Sofia Martinez: typical is 95p threshold at 1.5x baseline or an absolute ceiling (for you 250ms), and error rate threshold 1% over baseline for 5 minutes. for rollback we lock for 10 minutes then gradual rollback to 100% fallback.
12:30 Dr. Lian Chen: and what about data residency during the test? our PHI policy forbids using external hosted unless it's in our VPC. can we run the dry-run inside Private deployment or Dedicated?
12:46 Jordan Park: yes — for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated can be peered into your VPC and keep data on-net; Private (on-prem) is also possible but heavier. for the test we can run a Dedicated sandbox in your region.
13:30 Priya Rao: we are leaning Dedicated then, but need cost numbers.
13:37 Jordan Park: noted, we'll include cost scenarios in next deck.
14:05 Sofia Martinez: small caveat on model compatibility — not all model variants support int8 quantization or certain kernel optimizations, so fallback must be to a compatible architecture. our selector matrix includes compatibility tags (fp16, int8, q4).
15:00 Dr. Lian Chen: can you walk through a concrete example? say we pin rwd-30b-int8 and it degrades, where does traffic go?
15:12 Sofia Martinez: we'd map fallback to rwd-13b-fp16 first, then if that also fails, to rwd-7b-q4. we prefer stepdown by capacity to preserve UX while protecting throughput. critics: content fidelity drops, but we can flag longer answers as 'processing' and finish with best-effort.
16:05 Marcus Nguyen: any concerns about hallucinations when stepping down?
16:12 Sofia Martinez: yes risk increases; we recommend tying quality regression alerts to small eval prompt sets that you provide. if quality drops beyond tolerance we'll fail closed to a cached response or human-in-the-loop path.
17:00 Priya Rao: let's be explicit — acceptance criteria for POC: 95p < 250ms for triage path at 50 qps sustained; end-to-end throughput 200 qps for background tasks; quality delta less than 8% on top-50 evals when stepping from 30b->13b.
17:30 Dr. Lian Chen: ok that's written down.
18:10 Jordan Park: moving on — Sofia ran an additional stress test showing KV cache warmups improve median by 30% and 95p by ~20% for the 13b. we should config a 60s session affinity to keep KV warm for interactive routes.
18:50 Marcus Nguyen: session affinity has implications for autoscaling, will that increase idle GPU occupancy?
19:00 Sofia Martinez: slight increase but you get better tail latencies; autoscaler policies can be tuned to add burst nodes only when TTL of sessions exceeds threshold.
19:35 Dr. Lian Chen: any security signoffs needed to enable session affinity?
19:44 Jordan Park: nothing special, it's runtime config; from a security perspective Dedicated with private subnets and KMS is the primary ask.
20:12 Ethan Cole: quick procurement note — we'll package SOC2, ISO certs, and an appendix for PHI handling, and a short PCA list for your compliance team.
20:30 Priya Rao: thanks, that'll help.
21:05 Sofia Martinez: anything else on selector matrix? i want to show you the compatibility table — rwd-30b-int8 compatible with int8 kernels only on A100 v5 and above; 13b_fp16 is broadly compatible on older gen GPUs.
21:45 Marcus Nguyen: we run on GCP n2d with A100s, should be fine, i'll confirm GPU generation.
22:05 Dr. Lian Chen: also can we get trace-level logs for each request for later audit? we need redaction options for PHI fields.
22:22 Jordan Park: yes, audit logs + sampling traces available; redaction is configurable at ingestion and we support KMS-based tokenization. we'll send the doc.
23:00 Sofia Martinez: now on rollback dry-run logistics — propose target window 11/24 as Jordan said; we'll need you to approve a test plan and a blast radius (which routes are in scope).
23:22 Dr. Lian Chen: scope triage UI only for the dry-run, don't touch batch report pipelines.
23:30 Jordan Park: good, we'll draft a runbook and share.
24:15 Marcus Nguyen: how long do rollbacks typically take to route fully?
24:22 Sofia Martinez: routing changes are instant once the control plane flips; practical time to stabilize is 30-120s as KV warming and autoscaler react.
25:10 Priya Rao: what about rollback if a model has a schema change in tool-calling or function outputs?
25:22 Sofia Martinez: we validate output schema in the canary and shadow checks; if schema drift is detected we fail closed and route to a compatibility-safe variant or cached response. that's in the rollback playbook.
26:05 Dr. Lian Chen: good. any weirdness in metrics collection — i saw some missing labels in the CSV last week.
26:15 Sofia Martinez: noted, we had a small exporter bug that dropped a few request tags on old canaries; fixed and we'll re-upload clean data.
27:00 Jordan Park: quick note on costs again — fallback to a smaller model reduces token cost but may increase user time to resolution; we can model that economically in the sheet.
27:30 Priya Rao: acceptable, send the sheet.
28:20 Marcus Nguyen: curious — if we do warm-shadowing to compare 30b and 13b, does that double tokens charged?
28:30 Sofia Martinez: yes it increases units; we usually run limited warm-shadows for short windows to validate regressions, not continuously.
29:10 Dr. Lian Chen: anything else from SE perspective?
29:20 Sofia Martinez: i'll run the 100qps stress run with KV enabled and produce a histogram with 50/95/99 percentiles plus tail event logs. also i'll mark compatibility tags in the model catalog for your team.
30:02 Jordan Park: great. we'll also prepare a short checklist for your compliance folks and share the security appendix.
30:18 Priya Rao: thanks. on timeline — we aim to complete POC acceptance by end of November if dry-run goes well.
30:30 Jordan Park: that's doable if we hit these action items this week.
31:10 Dr. Lian Chen: quick nit — can we have an emergency unpin plan? say a hotfix must be deployed fast, what's the fastest safe route?
31:25 Sofia Martinez: yes, emergency unpin is control-plane flip + automatic rollback to last-known-good model version. we recommend pre-populating a 'safe list' of versions to ensure compatibility.
32:10 Marcus Nguyen: will that also rollback any feature flags we've toggled?
32:20 Sofia Martinez: feature flags are orthogonal, but we can bundle a play that flips both model pin and related flags atomically via our rollout API.
33:00 Jordan Park: ok we're at 33 minutes, let's recap next steps and owners.
33:10 Jordan Park: recap: Jordan to send SOC2/security pack and pricing; Sofia to run stress tests and update catalog compatibility tags; Marcus to give GPU generation and upload traces; Lian to confirm evals and acceptance SLOs; schedule dry-run 11/24.
33:45 Ethan Cole: i'll follow up with calendar invite and the draft runbook for the dry-run.
34:05 Priya Rao: thanks everyone.
34:30 Dr. Lian Chen: small note — competitor benchmarking would be useful, did you run Anthropic baseline?
34:45 Sofia Martinez: we ran a high-level external comparison for perf but can't share vendor raw logs; we can show relative deltas in the sheet.
35:20 Marcus Nguyen: ok fine.
36:00 Jordan Park: any blockers from HelixMed side?
36:05 Priya Rao: not really, just need the security pack and the final price to make a go/no-go decision.
36:20 Jordan Park: understood.
37:00 Sofia Martinez: one more technical thing — when we do the rollback dry-run we'll instrument an extra metric for 'model switch latency' to ensure user-visible switch is <2s, will include that in the runbook.
37:30 Dr. Lian Chen: perfect.
38:00 Jordan Park: all right, last check — are we okay to proceed with the plan and action items?
38:10 Marcus Nguyen: yes from infra.
38:12 Dr. Lian Chen: yes from data science.
38:15 Priya Rao: yes from product.
38:20 Jordan Park: thanks, we'll circulate notes and materials.
39:00 Ethan Cole: I'll attach the runbook and invite for 11/24 10:00 PT — tentative until Marcus confirms GPU types.
39:30 Priya Rao: thanks, looking forward.
40:00 Jordan Park: end call.

Post-call notes: runbook draft to be shared; stress run scheduled; SOC2 pack and pricing to be sent. minor transcription noise: 'kay-vee cache' sometimes transcribed weirdly; speaker labels may be approximate.
